faq.title: Frequently Asked Questions About Tax Accountants in Vancouver

items.question: Which tax service should I choose?
items.answer: Choose the service that matches your situation. Individuals and families usually need [personal tax](/personal-tax). Incorporated businesses need [corporate tax](/corporate-tax). Americans in Canada may need [cross-border tax](/us-cross-border), and executors need [estate tax](/trust-estate-tax). Not sure? Tell us your situation and we will point you to the right one.

items.question: Can LeadTax help with more than one service?
items.answer: Yes. Many clients combine services, such as personal and cross-border returns, or corporate tax and bookkeeping. Using one team keeps your records consistent, and your return reflects your whole financial picture instead of one slice of it. We confirm the scope of each service before work begins.

items.question: How are tax preparation fees determined?
items.answer: Fees depend on the service, the number of slips and accounts, and how complex your situation is. We confirm the scope and the fee before we start. Filing online yourself starts at $19 per return, and [bookkeeping plans](/bookkeeping) start at $199 per month. See current [pricing](/pricing) or call 1-877-453-2382.

items.question: What documents do I need to file my taxes in BC?
items.answer: Bring photo identification and your prior-year notice of assessment. Add every income slip, such as T4, T4A and T5, plus RRSP receipts and records for deductions you plan to claim. Landlords and self-employed clients also bring income and expense records. Tell us about any change in address, residency or family status.

items.question: When are Canadian personal tax returns due?
items.answer: For 2026 returns, most individuals must file and pay by April 30, 2027. Self-employed individuals and their spouses or partners have until June 15, 2027 to file, but any balance owing is still due April 30. Budget 2026 proposes a single May 15 deadline starting with 2027 returns, but that is a proposal and not yet law. See the [key tax dates](/tax-dates).

items.question: Can I file my taxes without visiting an office?
items.answer: Yes. LeadTax supports remote filing, document drop-off and online filing. You share your documents using a secure method we confirm with you, review the prepared return and approve it before we file. If you prefer a face-to-face visit, book an appointment at one of our Vancouver or Burnaby offices.

items.question: Do Americans living in Vancouver have to file US taxes?
items.answer: Generally yes. US citizens and green card holders must file a US return on worldwide income wherever they live, even when they owe no US tax after credits. Many also report foreign accounts. Our [cross-border tax team](/us-cross-border) prepares US and Canadian returns together.

items.question: What is the difference between a tax accountant and a bookkeeper?
items.answer: A bookkeeper records and reconciles your transactions during the year. A tax accountant uses those records to prepare returns and plan ahead. At LeadTax, [bookkeeping](/bookkeeping) and [corporate tax](/corporate-tax) work together, so your records are ready when it is time to file.

items.question: Can I file tax returns for previous years?
items.answer: Yes. We help with prior-year and overdue returns. Bring any slips you still have, and we will help you identify what is missing. Filing overdue returns can restore access to credits and benefits tied to filing, and it can limit further penalties and interest. Contact us to get started.

items.question: How do I find a reliable tax accountant near me in Vancouver or Burnaby?
items.answer: Look for a local office, clear fees agreed in advance and reviews from real clients. Check how the firm handles your specific situation, such as cross-border or corporate filing. Clients have left more than 360 reviews across our locations. You can read our Google reviews, visit an office from the list above or [contact LeadTax](/contact) to talk through your needs.
